value.text: So there's no ORM layer being used—the drivers are working directly with raw SQL. I should include the specific file paths where column mapping gets handled across the different database implementations in the store/db directory.

q15.

| Struct | Path |
|---|---|
| `store.User` | `store/user.go` (line 29) |
| `store.Attachment` | `store/attachment.go` (line 16) |
| `store.Reaction` | `store/reaction.go` (line 7) |

There's no ORM or `TableName()` method in this repo — the mapping is done by hand-written SQL in the per-database drivers, which is how I confirmed each pairing:

- `user`: `INSERT INTO user (...)` in `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (line 17), plus equivalents in `store/db/postgres/user.go` and `store/db/mysql/user.go` (line 18), all scanning into `store.User`.
- `attachment`: `INSERT INTO \`attachment\`` in `store/db/sqlite/attachment.go` (line 34) and `INSERT INTO attachment` / `FROM attachment` in `store/db/postgres/attachment.go` (lines 33 and 108), scanning into `store.Attachment`.
- `reaction`: `INSERT INTO \`reaction\`` in `store/db/sqlite/reaction.go` (line 16) and `store/db/postgres/reaction.go` (line 13), scanning into `store.Reaction`.

One thing worth flagging so you don't grab the wrong type: there are identically named `User`, `Attachment`, and `Reaction` structs in the generated protobuf API layer (`proto/gen/api/v1/user_service.pb.go`, `proto/gen/api/v1/attachment_service.pb.go`, `proto/gen/api/v1/memo_service.pb.go`). Those are wire/API types, not table models.
